body:
Fixes #209

External consumers currently receive npm 404 for every runtime workspace. This PR prepares all 19 public workspaces for their first Changesets minor release, verifies compatible sibling versions, and tests real production archive installation in an independent Vite/React app.

The new consumer regression also reproduces a worker packaging bug: Vite leaves `new globalThis.URL(...)` unchanged, so the default asynchronous network worker cannot load after bundling. Both worker entry paths now use the static `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` form that Vite rewrites into emitted assets.

- Packs every public workspace with normal lifecycle hooks; checks exports, README, LICENSE, generated icons, worker, attribution and dependency licenses.
- Installs all actual tarballs with production dependencies, removes staged source, and builds with the consumer's installed Vite without aliases or source patches.
- Browser coverage checks React rendering, settings defaults, generated icons, both asynchronous worker paths, the foreign inspector, accessibility, bundle warnings, browser exceptions and HTTP failures. Included in the existing Chromium/WebKit UI workflow.
- Reproduction and bootstrap instructions: `experiments/published-consumer/README.md`. No reporting-site source was copied or relicensed.

## Verification

Verified commit `e618b1cf94c3b2a12f095cb522ed7971203881c8`:

- Regression before the fix: the external consumer test fails with `Worker loading` instead of `Worker positioned 3 vertices`; after the fix it passes. The initial-release unit regression fails without the Changeset and passes with it.
- Archive checks cover all 19 staged version 0.1.0 packages with normal prepack hooks and production-only consumer installation.
- `npm test` passes in CI on Node 24 across Linux, macOS and Windows; the full Bun/Deno platform matrix also passes. Linux Node: 4,117 passed, 13 skipped, zero failures.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:duplication` pass locally and in CI; duplication is 2.79% against a 10% limit.
- The new archive browser regression passes in Chromium (26.2s) and WebKit (25.9s). Full browser suite: 535 passed; the additional repeated WebKit overlay matrix: 39 passed; native web keyboard/accessibility checks: 2 passed.
- All seven workflows are green: 48 successful checks, 12 conditional skips, no failures. [Checks and release](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/actions/runs/42321239529), [UI tests](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/actions/runs/42321239508).
- The branch contains current main, the full PR diff was reviewed, and the working tree is clean.

## Publication acceptance criterion remains blocked

- [x] Prepare versioned runtime releases with compatible sibling ranges.
- [x] Verify generated assets and licenses in actual archives.
- [x] Install and run the external archive consumer without a checkout at runtime.
- [ ] Publish all runtime packages to npm and verify a consumer installed from registry archives.

All 19 runtime package names still return npm 404. [Main run 42313474630](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/actions/runs/42313474630) fails release preflight (downloaded log lines 152–170): OIDC cannot bootstrap packages that do not yet exist. The repository Actions secrets API returns no secrets. A maintainer must provide a granular `NPM_TOKEN` authorized to create the packages and explicitly authorize the initial release; then configure trusted publishing for `release.yml`. This PR does not publish, merge, or declare that acceptance criterion complete. Local tarballs prove release contents and execution, not registry availability.

The separate inherited main lint failure is tracked in #219.

## Visual evidence

Before: the archive consumer remains at `Worker loading`.

![Before](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/issue-209-8d38d64ac08b/docs/screenshots/issue-209-before.png?raw=true)

After: both asynchronous worker paths run, the network renders and the inspector opens.

![After](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/issue-209-8d38d64ac08b/docs/screenshots/issue-209-after.png?raw=true)
title: Prepare initial runtime releases and verify external archive consumers
